text: Environmental novelty point relative conditions known presences, recipes step: quadratic SDM assessed spatial block cross-validation, Continuous Boyce Index True Skill Statistic:
code: library(recipes) library(parsnip)  rec <- recipe(presence ~ temp + rain + forest, data = inv_sdm_data) |>   step_inv_env_distance(temp, rain, forest, presence = presence)  bake(prep(rec), new_data = NULL) |>   dplyr::summarise(     mean_mahalanobis = mean(env_mahalanobis),     share_novel = mean(env_mess < 0),     .by = presence   ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   presence   mean_mahalanobis share_novel #>   <fct>                 <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1 background             3.98       0.573 #> 2 presence               1.58       0 spec <- inv_sdm(degree = 2) |> set_engine("glm")  set.seed(1) folds <- inv_spatial_block_cv(inv_sdm_data, lon = lon, lat = lat, v = 5,   block_size = 1.5)  scores <- lapply(folds$splits, function(split) {   train <- rsample::analysis(split)   test <- rsample::assessment(split)   fitted <- fit(spec, presence ~ temp + rain + forest, data = train)   preds <- dplyr::bind_cols(test, predict(fitted, test, type = "prob"),     predict(fitted, test))   dplyr::bind_rows(     boyce_index(preds, presence, .pred_presence),     tss(preds, presence, .pred_class)   ) }) dplyr::bind_rows(scores) |>   dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(.estimate, na.rm = TRUE), .by = .metric) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   .metric      mean #>   <chr>       <dbl> #> 1 boyce_index 0.712 #> 2 tss         0.597

title: Continuous Boyce Index — boyce_index
text: Continuous Boyce Index (CBI; Hirzel et al. 2006) evaluates presence-background presence-predictions. Moving windows width window_width (fraction prediction range) slid across predicted suitability. window ratio proportion presences proportion evaluation points (presences background) computed; index Spearman correlation window centre ratio. Values near 1 mean presences become frequent expected suitability rises; values near 0 mean model better random. Successive duplicate ratios removed computing correlation, reference implementation.

title: Rate of introduction from first records, allowing for discovery effort — inv_discovery_rate
text: number alien species first recorded year rises rate introduction effort put finding . Solow Costello (2004) separate two: species arrive rate \(\mu_t = \exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 t)\), undiscovered species found year t probability \(\pi_t = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\gamma_0 + \gamma_1 t)\), expected first records year t \(\lambda_t = \sum_{s \le t} \mu_s \pi_t \prod_{r=s}^{t-1}(1 - \pi_r)\). four parameters fitted Poisson maximum likelihood. positive beta_1 means introductions accelerating even allowing growing discovery effort; positive gamma_1 means detection improved. Time runs first year data, years first record included given rows count zero. two rates weakly separable short records; check widths intervals.
